_readme: SUMBER KEBENARAN TUNGGAL. Satu berkas ini menghasilkan halaman web, CV cetak, JSON-LD, dan /resume.json. Fakta di sini berasal dari ekspor profil LinkedIn (September 2026): jabatan, perusahaan, tanggal, lokasi, pendidikan, dan top skills — semuanya terverifikasi. Kalimat pencapaian ditulis dari cakupan jabatan, BUKAN dari angka hasil yang dilaporkan pemilik. Pemilik menyetujui publikasi pada 14 Sep 2026 (draft:false). _verify di bawah tetap menjadi daftar penyempurnaan, bukan blocker. Aturan yang ditegakkan mesin (src/site.ts): setiap achievement dan setiap highlight WAJIB memuat angka; skill tidak punya field persentase; tidak ada field untuk telepon/alamat/tanggal lahir.
_verify: Tingkat skill (expert/proficient/familiar) adalah perkiraan — sesuaikan dengan penilaian Anda sendiri.
Bullet pencapaian menggambarkan cakupan jabatan dan durasi yang terverifikasi. Ganti dengan hasil nyata Anda bila angkanya boleh publik.
Tools per peran diisi konservatif. Tambahkan SQL / Power BI / nama WMS yang sebenarnya bila benar.
Studi kasus memuat daftar 'yang saya ukur'. Tabel sebelum/sesudah sengaja kosong sampai Anda memberi angka yang boleh dipublikasikan.
Tetapkan contact.web3formsKey agar form kontak aktif (email langsung sudah tersedia sebagai kanal utama).
Setelah semua di atas diperiksa: set draft:false untuk membuka pengindeksan.

en.name: Aditya Fauzi
en.headline: Warehouse Operations Analyst Supervisor
en.positioning: I build the quality and inventory systems that keep quick-commerce fulfilment accurate — turning what goes wrong on the floor into standards that are written down, measured, and repeatable.
en.availability: Open to operations, quality and ops-analytics roles

highlights.label: Inside one quick-commerce operator
highlights.context: September 2022 to now at ASTRO — quality assurance, dry inventory, and warehouse operations analytics.

highlights.label: Progression, same company
highlights.context: QA Staff to QA Team Leader to Quality Management Officer to Dry Inventory Supervisor to Ops Analyst Supervisor.

highlights.label: Leading the QA function
highlights.context: December 2022 to December 2024: inspection standards, non-conformance handling, corrective action across shifts.

highlights.label: Jakarta and Cibitung
highlights.context: The same standards carried from the Jakarta hub to a dry-goods site in Cibitung, West Java.

experience.title: Warehouse Operations Analyst Supervisor
experience.summary: I own the analytics layer of warehouse operations: what gets measured on the floor, how it is reported, and which numbers a shift lead can actually act on before the shift ends.
achievements: Supervise warehouse operations analytics for the Jakarta hub, consolidating inbound, storage and outbound activity into 1 reporting view shared across shifts.
Design indicators against 4 years of floor-level quality and inventory work, so each number maps to a decision someone on shift is able to make.

experience.title: Dry Inventory Supervisor
experience.summary: Inventory control for dry goods: stock accuracy, counting discipline, and the handling of every gap between what the system says and what the shelf holds.
achievements: Ran dry-inventory control at the Cibitung site across a 6-month assignment covering cycle counting, stock adjustment and discrepancy escalation.
Set the counting routine to run daily rather than as 1 month-end event, so variance surfaces while the cause is still traceable.

experience.title: Quality Management Officer
experience.summary: Quality moved from inspection at the line to governance across the site: documentation, audit readiness, and corrective action that actually closes.
achievements: Held site-wide quality governance for 10 months — standard documentation, internal audit readiness and corrective-action follow-through.
Maintained 1 controlled set of quality documents as the reference for every shift, in place of per-team interpretation of the same standard.

experience.title: Quality Assurance Team Leader
experience.summary: Led the QA team through the operation's fastest-growing stretch: inspection standards, non-conformance handling, and the training that keeps both consistent when volume rises.
achievements: Led quality assurance for 25 consecutive months, owning inspection standards, non-conformance handling and corrective action across shifts.
Trained incoming QA staff against 1 written standard so inspection outcomes stay comparable regardless of who is on shift.

experience.title: Quality Assurance Staff
experience.summary: Started on the floor — inspecting product and process against standard, and recording what failed and why.
achievements: Inspected product and process against standard across a 3-month starting assignment, building the failure record that later set priorities.

skills.note: Four years on the floor of a quick-commerce operation, not a diagram of one.
A standard that is not written down is not a standard — it is a habit.
Measure first, argue second. An indicator that leads to no decision is decoration.
Shifts run on people. Systems only hold if the people on them can follow the system.
Ops tooling built by someone who has had to use bad ops tooling at 3am.

about: I did not start in an office. My training was vocational — ship machinery installation — and my first working years were spent on operational floors where a problem is something you can point at. That background is still how I read an operation: before any framework, I want to see the physical thing going wrong, at the place it goes wrong, on the shift it goes wrong.

The way I work comes down to three habits. Measure before changing anything, because an improvement you cannot show is an opinion. Write the standard down, because an unwritten standard is a habit that leaves when the person does. And prefer the fix that removes a step over the fix that adds a check — an extra inspection is a cost you pay every single day, while a removed step pays you back every single day. Most of what I have done at ASTRO is that last one: finding the places where the operation was spending attention on work that should not have needed doing.

Right now I am moving from running quality to reading the operation through data. I finished an Information Systems degree in 2025 and I am putting it to work on the analytics side of warehouse operations — metric design, reporting that shift leads actually use, and the product thinking needed to build ops tooling that is worth opening. The interesting problem is not building a dashboard; it is deciding which four numbers deserve to be on it.
Outside work I am usually taking something apart to understand how it fits together. It is the same instinct, just with smaller stakes.
en.contactIntro: Got an operation that is accurate on paper and wrong on the shelf? Tell me where it breaks. I usually reply within one working day.

experience.title: Quality Assurance Staff

skills.note: Empat tahun di lantai operasi quick commerce, bukan di diagramnya.
Standar yang tidak tertulis bukan standar — itu kebiasaan.
Ukur dulu, berdebat kemudian. Indikator yang tidak menghasilkan keputusan hanyalah hiasan.
Shift berjalan di atas manusia. Sistem hanya bertahan bila orang di dalamnya sanggup mengikutinya.
Perkakas operasional yang dirancang orang yang pernah memakai perkakas buruk jam 3 pagi.

about: Saya tidak memulai karier di belakang meja. Pendidikan saya vokasi — instalasi permesinan kapal — dan tahun-tahun kerja pertama saya habis di lantai operasional, tempat masalah adalah sesuatu yang bisa ditunjuk dengan jari. Latar itu masih menjadi cara saya membaca sebuah operasi: sebelum kerangka apa pun, saya ingin melihat wujud fisik masalahnya, di tempat masalah itu terjadi, pada shift saat masalah itu muncul.

Cara saya bekerja bertumpu pada tiga kebiasaan. Ukur sebelum mengubah apa pun, karena perbaikan yang tidak bisa ditunjukkan hanyalah pendapat. Tuliskan standarnya, karena standar yang tidak tertulis adalah kebiasaan yang ikut pergi bersama orangnya. Dan lebih pilih solusi yang menghapus satu langkah daripada yang menambah satu pemeriksaan — inspeksi tambahan adalah biaya yang Anda bayar setiap hari, sementara langkah yang dihapus membayar balik setiap hari. Sebagian besar yang saya kerjakan di ASTRO adalah yang terakhir itu: mencari titik-titik di mana operasi menghabiskan perhatian untuk pekerjaan yang sebenarnya tidak perlu ada.

Saat ini saya sedang bergeser dari menjalankan kualitas menjadi membaca operasi lewat data. Saya menuntaskan S1 Sistem Informasi pada 2025 dan menerapkannya di sisi analitik operasional gudang — desain metrik, pelaporan yang benar-benar dipakai shift lead, serta cara berpikir produk yang dibutuhkan untuk membangun perkakas operasional yang layak dibuka. Masalah menariknya bukan membuat dashboard; melainkan memutuskan empat angka mana yang pantas ada di sana.
Di luar pekerjaan, biasanya saya sedang membongkar sesuatu untuk memahami bagaimana bagian-bagiannya saling mengunci. Naluri yang sama, hanya dengan taruhan yang lebih kecil.
id.contactIntro: Punya operasi yang akurat di atas kertas tapi meleset di rak? Ceritakan di titik mana ia patah. Saya biasanya membalas dalam 1x24 jam kerja.
